source_text: Σὺ δὲ μάθε τὴν »καθ᾿ ὑπερβολὴν ὁδόν«, ἣν δείκνυσι Παῦλος ἐπὶ σωτηρίαν· »ἡ ἀγάπη τὰ ἑαυτῆς οὐ ζητεῖ«, ἀλλ᾿ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἐκκέχυται· περὶ τοῦτον ἐπτόηται, περὶ τοῦτον σωφρόνως μαίνεται. »ἀγάπη καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν· ἡ τελεία ἀγάπη ἐκβάλλει τὸν φόβον· οὐ περπερεύεται, οὐ φυσιοῦται. οὐκ ἐπιχαίρει τῇ ἀδικίᾳ, συγχαίρει δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ· πάντα στέγει. πάντα πιστεύει, πάντα ἐλπίζει. πάντα ὑπομένει. ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε ἐκπίπτει, προφητεῖαι καταργοῦνται. γλῶσσαι παύονται, ἰάσεις ἐπὶ γῆς καταλείπονται. μένει δὲ τὰ τρία ταῦτα, πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀγάπη· μείζων δὲ ἐν τούτοις ἡ ἀγάπη.« καὶ δικαίως· πίστις μὲν γὰρ ἀπέρχεται, ὅταν αὐτοψίᾳ πεισθῶμεν ἰδόντες θεόν, καὶ ἐλπὶς ἀφανίζεται τῶν ἐλπισθέντων ἀποδοθέντων, ἀγάπη δὲ εἰς πλήρωμα συνέρχεται καὶ μᾶλλον αὔξεται τῶν τελείων παραδοθέντων. ἐὰν ταύτην ἐμβάληταί τις τῇ ψυχῇ, δύναται, κἂν ἐν ἁμαρτήμασιν ᾖ γεγεννημένος, κἂν πολλὰ τῶν κεκωλυμένων εἰργασμένος, αὐξήσας τὴν ἀγάπην καὶ μετάνοιαν καθαρὰν λαβὼν ἀναμαχέσασθαι τὰ ἐπταισμένα.
thought_title: Love as the surpassing way that remains
orientation: Clement is addressing the reader directly, showing from Paul and 1 John that love is the surpassing way to salvation, the one thing that remains when faith and hope pass away.
pass_a_gloss: But you, learn the way according to excess, which Paul points out for salvation: love does not seek its own things, but is poured out upon the brother; about this one it is in ecstasy, about this one it rages soberly. Love covers a multitude of sins; perfect love casts out fear; it does not boast, it is not puffed up. It does not rejoice at unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; it bears all things. It believes all things, hopes all things. It endures all things. Love never falls away; prophecies are abolished. Tongues cease; healings are left behind upon the earth. But these three remain, faith, hope, love; and greater among these is love. And justly so: for faith departs, when we are persuaded by seeing with our own eyes, having seen God, and hope disappears when the things hoped for are given back, but love comes together into fullness and increases all the more when the perfect things are handed over. If someone casts this love into the soul, he is able, even if he has been born in sins, even if he has worked many of the forbidden things, having increased the love and having received pure repentance, to fight back against the things he has stumbled in.

lemmas.gloss: are abolished, are done away with
to fight back against, to win back by fighting

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Pauline phrase; 'excess' preserves the sense of surpassing or extraordinary without importing the polished 'more excellent way' of existing translations.
The verb πτοέω means to be in a state of passionate excitement or alarm; 'is in ecstasy' captures the intense emotional focus on the brother without the negative connotation of 'terrified.'
The oxymoron is deliberate in Clement; keeping both words literal preserves the paradox of love's madness being self-controlled.

choices.english: healings are left behind upon the earth
choices.why: Literal rendering; 'left behind' preserves the sense that healings are abandoned or remain behind as inferior things when the perfect comes.

choices.english: casts this love into the soul
choices.why: The verb ἐμβάλλω means to throw or cast in; keeping 'casts' preserves the active, forceful image of implanting love.

choices.english: to fight back against the things he has stumbled in
choices.why: The compound ἀναμάχομαι means to renew a fight or win back by fighting; 'fight back against' preserves the military metaphor and the sense of recovering from past stumbles.
rejected: to make amends for his stumbles

pass_b_english: But you, learn the way according to excess that Paul points to for salvation. "Love does not seek its own things," but is poured out upon the brother. It is frantic for him, and soberly raves for him. "Love covers a multitude of sins" (1 Peter 4:8). "Perfect love casts out fear" (1 John 4:18). "It does not boast; it is not puffed up. It does not rejoice in wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails. Prophecies are abolished; tongues cease; healings are left behind upon the earth. But these three remain: faith, hope, love; and the greatest of these is love" (1 Corinthians 13:4-8, 13). And rightly so. For faith departs when we are persuaded by seeing God with our own eyes, and hope vanishes when the things hoped for are handed over. But love comes together into fullness and grows all the more when the perfect things are handed over. If someone casts this love into his soul, he can—even if he was born in sins, even if he has done many of the things that are forbidden—grow the love, receive pure repentance, and fight back against the things he has done wrong.

problems.quote: fight back against the things he has stumbled in.
problems.why: ἀναμαχέσασθαι means 'fight back against' but the object τὰ ἐπταισμένα are 'the things gone wrong / sins committed', not 'things stumbled in'.
problems.fix: fight back against the things he has done wrong.
problems.ruling: Misrepresents ἀναμαχέσασθαι τὰ ἐπταισμένα as 'stumbled in' rather than 'combat the sins/offenses'.

edits.old: fight back against the things he has stumbled in.
edits.new: fight back against the things he has done wrong.

fixed: Changed 'stumbled in' to 'done wrong' for τὰ ἐπταισμένα, which refers to sins committed, not stumbling.

problems.quote: It is in ecstasy over him; it rages soberly over him.
problems.source_quote: περὶ τοῦτον ἐπτόηται, περὶ τοῦτον σωφρόνως μαίνεται.
problems.why: Greek says love is poured out on him and is restrained soberly, not ‘ecstatic’ or ‘raging’.
problems.fix: It is poured out upon him, and is restrained soberly toward him.

edits.old: It is in ecstasy over him; it rages soberly over him.
edits.new: It is poured out upon him, and is restrained soberly toward him.

fixed: Changed 'It is in ecstasy over him; it rages soberly over him.' to 'It is poured out upon him, and is restrained soberly toward him.' because the Greek 'περὶ τοῦτον ἐπτόηται, περὶ τοῦτον σωφρόνως μαίνεται' describes love as poured out and soberly restrained, not ecstatic or raging.

problems.quote: It is poured out upon him, and is restrained soberly toward him.
problems.source_quote: περὶ τοῦτον ἐπτόηται, περὶ τοῦτον σωφρόνως μαίνεται
problems.why: ἐπτόηται means 'is frantic/insane', not 'restrained'; σωφρόνως μαίνεται is 'soberly raves', a paradox, not 'restrained soberly'.
problems.fix: It is frantic for him, and soberly raves for him.
problems.ruling: Greek ἐπτόηται = 'is terrified/astonished', not 'poured out'; σωφρόνως μαινεται = 'soberly raves', not 'restrained soberly', altering meaning.

edits.old: It is poured out upon him, and is restrained soberly toward him.
edits.new: It is frantic for him, and soberly raves for him.

fixed: The source περὶ τοῦτον ἐπτόηται, περὶ τοῦτον σωφρόνως μαίνεται means 'about this one it is in ecstasy, about this one it rages soberly.' The English 'restrained soberly' misstates σωφρόνως μαίνεται, which is a paradox of sober madness, not restraint. Changed to 'It is frantic for him, and soberly raves for him.'

last_rejected.quote: It is frantic for him, and soberly raves for him.
last_rejected.source_quote: περὶ τοῦτον ἐπτόηται, περὶ τοῦτον σωφρόνως μαίνεται.
last_rejected.why: Greek says ‘eager for him, and soberly cares for him’; English mis‑renders as ‘frantic… raves’, changing meaning.
last_rejected.fix: It is eager for him, and soberly cares for him.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπτόηται means frantic/agitated; μαίνεται means raves/mad. σωφρόνως is adverb. English captures the paradox correctly.

last_rejected.quote: hope vanishes when the things hoped for are handed over.
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ἐλπὶς ἀφανίζεται τῶν ἐλπισθέντων ἀποδοθέντων
last_rejected.why: Greek means ‘hope disappears when those who hoped are handed over’; English shifts agency to ‘things hoped for’.
last_rejected.fix: and hope disappears when those who have hoped are handed over.
last_rejected.ruling: τῶν ἐλπισθέντων are neuter plural 'things hoped for,' not people. ἀποδοθέντων = handed over. English is correct.

last_rejected.quote: when the perfect things are handed over
last_rejected.why: Greek refers to ‘the perfect ones (people) being handed over’; English mistakenly says ‘perfect things’.
last_rejected.fix: when the perfect ones are handed over
last_rejected.ruling: τῶν τελείων is neuter plural, 'the perfect things,' not masculine persons. English rendering is grammatically correct.
